questions.question: Which header typically carries an authentication token on an API request?
questions.explanation: The Authorization header carries credentials, e.g. 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'. Content-Type and Accept describe formats, not identity.

questions.question: In the URL /todos?userId=1, what is userId=1?
questions.explanation: Anything appended after a '?' is a query parameter, typically used to filter, sort, or page results.

questions.question: In the URL /todos/1, what is the 1?
options: A path parameter identifying a specific resource
questions.explanation: The 1 is part of the URL's structure itself, identifying which specific todo to act on — that makes it a path parameter.

questions.question: Which part of an HTTP response tells you whether the request succeeded?
questions.explanation: The status code (e.g. 200, 404, 500) is the definitive signal of outcome — always check it before trusting the body.

questions.question: Why should you set Content-Type when sending a request with a body?
options: It's purely cosmetic and has no effect
It tells the receiver what format to expect the body in, so it can parse it correctly
It changes the HTTP method being used
It's only needed for GET requests
questions.explanation: Content-Type tells the receiving server how to interpret the body (e.g. application/json) — omit it and many APIs will misinterpret or reject the request.
